summary: When you type a command, bash looks for it in each folder listed in PATH. Add a folder to PATH to run your own scripts by name, and use alias to give a long command a short name.
notes: export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH" puts ~/bin first and keeps every folder that was already there. It lasts until you close the terminal. Add the line to ~/.bashrc to keep it.
Aliases also last only for this session. Put alias ll='ls -l' in ~/.bashrc so every new terminal has it.
shopt -s expand_aliases is only needed because this page runs your commands from a script. In a terminal you type in, aliases work without it.
pitfall: export PATH="$HOME/bin" without :$PATH replaces the whole list, and then even ls fails with ls: command not found. Close the terminal and open a new one to get the old PATH back.
